IG + AS

What does the microphone actually give us?

Microphone → analogue electrical signal → ADC → binary sample values.
Analogue data vary continuously. Digital data use discrete encoded values. A microphone produces a voltage responding to pressure; the ADC performs conversion.
① Measure amplitude at regular intervals. ② Quantise to an available amplitude level. ③ Encode each value in binary and store the sequence.
📝 IN THE EXAMUse the stated model, precise terms and requested units.
🏛 IN REALITYMicrophones and converters have bandwidth, noise and other limits. No physical device copies a signal exactly.
IG + AS

Noise changes a voltage. Must it change the bit?

📝 IN THE EXAMDigital values can be regenerated when received signals remain within the correct decision region.
🏛 IN REALITYTwo carrier models are shown, not two complete recordings. A decision error need not destroy every bit.
SHARED ENRICHMENT

↓ What survives a noisy copy?

Predict: can a digital copy preserve its values even though its physical voltage was disturbed?
In our two-level model, the receiver decides between −1 and +1 using a threshold at 0. Noise smaller than the margin cannot cross that threshold.
Yes, the recovered values can remain exact. Cross a threshold and individual bits may change. Real systems add timing recovery and error detection/correction; they do not guarantee immunity to arbitrary noise.
📝 IN THE EXAMOptional investigation, not an additional exam method.
🏛 IN REALITYOur model isolates one mechanism. Real capture, storage and playback add other constraints.

IG + AS

The first dial — how often?

Sample rate: number of samples taken per second, measured in Hz.
Closer time spacing can capture faster changes. Predict which musical details change when the rate is reduced.

Ready · same 15-second excerpt

Controlled comparison: same reference, mono, 15 seconds and 16-bit amplitude precision. Rate reduction includes anti-alias filtering.
📝 IN THE EXAMBoth boards ask for sample rate and its effects on accuracy and data size.
🏛 IN REALITYFiltering removes frequencies the lower rate cannot represent safely; unfiltered undersampling can create aliases.
SHARED ENRICHMENT

↓ Why not a neat 40,000?

A signal limited to below 20 kHz needs a sample rate above 40 kHz for ideal reconstruction. Practical filters need room to transition.
Predict: does the theorem select exactly 44,100?
No. Sony’s PCM-1610 recorded digital audio through video equipment and offered 44.1 kHz and 44.056 kHz. Practical compatibility helped shape the standards; the theorem alone does not choose one exact rate.

Historical source: Sony PCM-1610 product brochure. Its marketing absolutes are not adopted here.

📝 IN THE EXAMOptional investigation, not an additional exam method.
🏛 IN REALITYThe ideal theorem assumes band-limited signals and exact samples; real converters add other limits.

↓ Two waves, one set of samples

Red: 7 Hz. Sample rate: 8 Hz. Predict what low-frequency wave fits the same sample times.

A 1 Hz wave with reversed phase fits the same ideal samples. Without a bandwidth constraint, those samples cannot identify which wave was present. Anti-alias filters restrict the input first.

IG + AS

The second dial — how precisely?

Sample resolution: bits used for each sample. n bits permit 2ⁿ codes/levels in this model.
Quantisation maps amplitude to an allowed level. A coarser grid can produce larger rounding errors.

Ready · same 15-second excerpt

Controlled comparison: 48 kHz, mono,15 seconds. Only quantisation changes; no dither is added. Listen for distortion/noise, especially in quieter passages.
📝 IN THE EXAMUse the stated model, precise terms and requested units.
🏛 IN REALITYThese lossless files carry 16-bit samples. “4 bits” describes the processing grid, not the container width.

SHARED ENRICHMENT

↓ Is “8-bit music” an 8-bit recording?

Predict: are instructions that generate pulse/triangle/noise sounds the same representation as stored microphone samples?
Synthesis generates a waveform from instructions; recorded audio stores measurements. Chiptune style does not specify one PCM bit depth. NES tools support both synthesis channels and a DPCM sample channel—so “there were no samples” is false.

Primary developer source: Neil Baldwin’s NTRQ manual, sound channels and DPCM.

📝 IN THE EXAMOptional investigation, not an additional exam method.
🏛 IN REALITYOur model isolates one mechanism. Real capture, storage and playback add other constraints.

IG + AS

Count samples. Then count bits.

Samples/second × seconds × bits/sample × channels = bits.
÷8 gives bytes. ÷1024 gives KiB; ÷1024² gives MiB. For mono, channels=1.
Worked model: 32,000 Hz ×12 s ×16 bits ×1 =6,144,000 bits
÷8 =768,000 bytes; ÷1024 =750 KiB.
📝 IN THE EXAMUse the stated model, precise terms and requested units.
🏛 IN REALITYThe formula counts packed, uncompressed PCM data. Headers, compression and container padding can change file size.

DECLARE RateChoice, DepthChoice, Rate, Bits, Seconds : INTEGER
DECLARE KiB, Rounded : REAL
Seconds ← 30
FOR RateChoice ← 1 TO 3
    CASE OF RateChoice
        1 : Rate ← 8000
        2 : Rate ← 22050
        3 : Rate ← 44100
    ENDCASE
    FOR DepthChoice ← 1 TO 3
        CASE OF DepthChoice
            1 : Bits ← 4
            2 : Bits ← 8
            3 : Bits ← 16
        ENDCASE
        KiB ← Rate * Bits * Seconds / 8 / 1024

AS 9618

AS: the prefix changes the divisor

Same raw data: 48,000 Hz ×16 bits ×25 s ×1 channel =19,200,000 bits =2,400,000 bytes.
In MB: ÷1,000,000 =2.4 MB.
In MiB: ÷1,048,576 ≈2.289 MiB.
Use the unit requested. A sound-size mark scheme can award one method point plus one answer point.

IG + AS

Name the dial, then explain its effect

ChangeRaw data sizePotential accuracy effect
Rate increasesIncreasesCloser times; captures faster changes
Bits/sample increaseIncreasesFiner amplitude levels; smaller rounding errors
Duration doublesDoublesSame precision, more time recorded
Channels 1→2DoublesA second signal, not finer samples
📝 IN THE EXAMBoth boards examine size and accuracy. Give the effect and a mechanism relevant to the question.
🏛 IN REALITYIncreasing rate does not by itself reduce the amplitude quantiser’s step. Benefits depend on the signal and processing.
IG + AS

A better recording—or a bigger copy?

A higher-rate new capture can retain faster changes, if the microphone and converter support them. A finer amplitude grid can retain smaller differences.
Resampling an existing file cannot by itself identify information already discarded. Extra stored values may be interpolated or padded.
Higher rates and depths can have production uses, but audibility depends on the signal, system and listener.192 kHz streaming exists; “nobody uses it” is not an explanation.
📝 IN THE EXAMUse the stated model, precise terms and requested units.
🏛 IN REALITYAn ideal converter’s roughly 6 dB-per-bit trend is not a universal “noise 96 dB below any music” guarantee.
AS 9618

AS: describe the amplitude error

A finite sample resolution gives a finite set of representable amplitudes.
An input amplitude between levels is mapped to a nearby available level. The difference is quantisation error.
More bits can provide more levels and smaller errors for the same amplitude range.
For rate questions, use smaller time gaps / closer representation of the waveform. Keep amplitude-grid explanations attached to resolution.
📝 IN THE EXAMUse the mechanism actually asked for. The scheme may allow several alternatives; do not count keywords.
🏛 IN REALITYSampling time and amplitude quantisation are distinct. Some published wording blurs them; the accepted time-gap answer avoids that conflation.
